incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in a system left unpatched for two years and dwelled in the network for over a week before deploying ransomware.
incidents.impact: Latvia's state forestry firm's mapping, hunting and contractor systems were knocked offline and ~44GB of data (documents, source code, certificates, keys, credentials) was leaked; two-thirds of contract customers still lacked access weeks later. The same actor also breached pharma firm Olpha.

incidents.vector: A Golang backdoor ('GigaWiper') bundles multiple destructive modules — a physical-disk wiper, fake ransomware derived from Crucio, and reimplemented FlockWiper logic — invoked as on-demand command-and-control commands.
incidents.impact: Wipes physical disks, removes partition tables and irrecoverably encrypts files with unsaved keys; Microsoft has observed it wiping compromised environments since October 2025.

incidents.vector: The Hyadina RaaS operation used a Microsoft-signed malicious kernel driver (PoisonX) in a bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver attack to kill security software, alongside AnyDesk RMM, 14 open-source credential stealers and PsExec.
incidents.impact: Endpoint defenses were disabled and credentials stolen before the group deployed its new 'GodDamn' ransomware locker at a US victim organization.

incidents.vector: A ransomware negotiator secretly leaked clients' negotiating positions and insurance limits to BlackCat/ALPHV affiliates and colluded to deploy ransomware.
incidents.impact: Insider Angelo Martino was sentenced to 70 months after helping extort a combined $75.3M from five US firms he was hired to protect; ~$10M in assets was seized.

incidents.vector: Mass scanning and exploitation of known CMS and plugin vulnerabilities (WordPress plugins, Craft CMS, Joomla JCE and others) enabling unauthenticated file upload, RCE and deserialization to plant webshells.
incidents.impact: Webshells give remote control of web servers for defacement, credential capture, malware hosting and network pivoting; many Australian SMBs impacted in an ASD/ACSC 'critical' alert.

incidents.vector: Actor UAT-7810 exploits known n-day vulnerabilities in unpatched Ruckus and ASUS routers to deploy upgraded LONGLEASH and DOGLEASH backdoors.
incidents.impact: Builds resilient Operational Relay Box (ORB) proxy networks that let other state-linked groups mask their origins when attacking high-value targets.

incidents.vector: Coordinated global law enforcement action against social-engineering scams (business email compromise, romance, investment and sextortion schemes) and money laundering.
incidents.impact: Interpol's Operation First Light produced 5,800+ arrests across 97 countries, $293M seized and 31,000+ bank accounts blocked.

incidents.vector: Brute-forced an externally exposed AWS EC2 instance hosting an AI gateway connected to Amazon Bedrock, then deployed the XMRig cryptominer.
incidents.impact: Used for cryptomining, but the gateway's broad permissions could have exposed model data, API keys, secrets and IAM roles — a potential 'mini supply chain' compromise.

incidents.victim: UK Foreign Office & 80,000+ Fortinet device owners
incidents.vector: Mass password spraying and credential theft ('FortiBleed') against internet-exposed Fortinet, Sophos and MSSQL services, followed by device-config extraction and offline password cracking.
incidents.impact: Credentials from ~80,000 Fortinet devices were stolen; VPN/firewall credentials for the UK Foreign Office, British embassies and local councils are being sold as a $60,000 archive by an actor calling itself 'SantaAd'.

incidents.vector: A lone attacker used agentic AI workflows to accelerate reconnaissance and tooling after stealing an AWS access key via a weakness in an internet-facing application, chaining flaws across apps, AWS resources, CI/CD pipelines and code repositories.
incidents.impact: Compromised a large AWS environment in roughly 72 hours, harvested secrets, planted backdoors and staged reversible disruption (blocking S3, zeroing ECS services) to extort the victim.

incidents.vector: Operators used leased Taiwanese LINE accounts to impersonate journalists, build trust with targets, then delivered malware disguised as encrypted-messaging software.
incidents.impact: Two Taiwanese businessmen were charged for leasing LINE accounts to a CCP-linked firm as part of a broad Beijing-linked phishing campaign against politicians, academics, journalists and civil society.

incidents.vector: Unusual activity was detected in a cloud account tied to one of Nayax's subsidiaries and was immediately blocked and contained.
incidents.impact: The Israeli payments company disclosed the cloud account compromise via an SEC 6-K; it says core production systems were unaffected and does not currently believe material information was exposed.

incidents.vector: FBI, IRS-CI and industry partners seized hundreds of domains behind the NetNut residential proxy service and its Popa botnet, which hijacked ~2 million consumer devices such as smart TVs and streaming boxes.
incidents.impact: The botnet relayed content-scraping, ad-fraud, account-takeover and criminal/espionage traffic; its infrastructure was seized and Google disabled linked accounts and apps.

incidents.vector: A malicious governance attack diverted 4.4 trillion BONK tokens to attacker-controlled wallets.
incidents.impact: Roughly $20 million in crypto assets were stolen; Upbit and Kraken paused BONK transactions during the investigation.

incidents.vector: Website defacement via 404-page hijacking.
incidents.impact: Multiple US Army websites were defaced with pro-Kurdish messages and insults directed at President Trump and the US Ambassador to Turkey.

incidents.vector: Malvertising lured victims to fake cracked-software downloads delivering a Factory-v3 Go loader — signed with a fabricated JustWatch certificate and inflated with null bytes to evade sandboxes — that drops Vidar stealer and the XMRig miner.
incidents.impact: Steals browser credentials, cookies and crypto wallets and mines Monero; Unit 42 identified 43 loader samples in an April 2026 campaign against US and EU victims.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack on a major Japanese telecommunications provider (technical details limited).
incidents.impact: The provider said the attack exposed approximately 12 million emails.

incidents.victim: Transport for London (+ SSM Health, Sutter Health)
incidents.vector: SIM-swapping and voice/SMS social-engineering intrusions; the group's August 2024 attack crippled Transport for London's systems.
incidents.impact: Two Scattered Spider members pleaded guilty over the TfL attack (one also admitted hacking US healthcare providers); the group is tied to 120 intrusions and $115M in ransoms, and another member was extradited to the US.

incidents.vector: Russian intelligence actors impersonate messaging-app support accounts to phish verification codes, PINs and Backup Recovery Keys for Signal, WhatsApp and Telegram accounts.
incidents.impact: Compromises individual accounts to read historical, private and group messages of high-value targets including figures in Ukraine; FBI/CISA updated their PSA (activity tracked as UNC5792 and UNC4221).

incidents.victim: John Bolton (former US National Security Advisor)
incidents.vector: An Iran-linked cyber actor hacked Bolton's personal email account after he left office in 2019; the account contained classified 'diary' notes he had transmitted to family members.
incidents.impact: Sensitive national-defense information was exposed to a foreign adversary; Bolton pleaded guilty to willfully retaining national defense information under the Espionage Act.
